To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AM fungus R. irregularis and silicon application modulate growth, proline biosythesis and yield in pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) genotypes (metal-sensitive and metal-tolerant) under Cd and Zn stress.
Si and/or AM modulate growth, nutrient, and water status, proline biosynthetic pathway and productivity of pigeonpea genotypic variants under heavy metal stress.

Si and/or AM could alleviate Cd and Zn phytotoxicity in pigeonpea by improving nutrient status, growth and yield, and Si application along with AM was more beneficial for growth, nutrient, yield and proline biosynthesis under both heavy metals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Si and/or AM in alleviating heavy metal stress in pigeonpea.

the role of Si and AM symbiosis in modulating growth and yield in two genotypes of pigeonpea under heavy metal stress and provides a basis for further studies on mycorrhizae-mediated heavy metal phytoremediation.
the potential of mycorrhiza and Si to improve the growth, nutrient acquisition and yield of pigeonpea under Cd and Zn stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AM is more effective than Si alone in improving growth, nutrient status, proline biosythesis and productivity under heavy metal stress in pigeonpea.
AM and Si have the potential to improve growth, proline biosynthetic capacity and productivity of pigeonpea under Cd and Zn stress.
Si and AM can ameliorate the phytotoxicity and improve the growth and productivity of pigeonpea under heavy metal stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined application of Si and AM could be used as a potential strategy to alleviate heavy metal toxicity in legumes.
Si application in combination with AM is a promising strategy for alleviating Cd and Zn stress in pigeonpea.
AM and Si can be effectively utilized to mitigate the adverse impacts of Zn and Cd on growth, nutrient and yield in pigeonpea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Si+AM could be a promising strategy to improve the growth and productivity of pigeonpea under heavy metal stress.
Si and AM could be used as a sustainable strategy to improve growth, nutrient uptake and productivity in pigeonpea genotypic under Cd and Zn stress.
AM and Si are beneficial for growth, nutrient and proline status and productivity of legumes under heavy metal stress and can be effectively used in metal contaminated soils.
